races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden
Matchbook Exchange Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Tally-Ho Stud Irish EBF Ballyogan Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Chantez
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground (10/10 similar-going runs) with a solid second-season profile, but Gary Carroll faces a positioning puzzle — this mare's natural instinct is to race up with the pace yet the sheer number of prominent types means she may find herself further back than suits, blunting her effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: William Haggas's sprinter is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field, carrying a career-high OR of 105 and recording her only 6f win on Soft, so the Good ground is a slight query; Cieren Fallon will need a strong gallop to deliver her late run and a compressed pace scenario could leave her with too much to do.|

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Kate McGivern's mare ran just nine days ago and has been busy throughout the season; she has strong Good-ground form (12/14) over six furlongs but her finishing positions have been modest in similar company, and Chris Hayes will likely anchor her at the back with limited expectation of a winning run.|

runners_data.name: Treasure Rose
runners_data.note: Johnny Murtagh's filly has won twice recently and is capable at this level, but she's a horse that needs to travel prominently — the overcrowded early tier in this field means Ben Coen may struggle to get her into the position where she's won before, and that positional compromise is her chief risk.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old arrives on the back of back-to-back wins over six furlongs and is the most upwardly mobile horse in the race; Declan McDonogh can slot him into a natural tracking role just off Havana Anna, which is the ideal position given the race shape, and his sim-going record on Good is solid.|

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: A genuine pace-liker by nature, Seamie Heffernan is unlikely to find front-running space with Havana Anna taking that role — Focaccia's best form has come when bowling along in front or very close to the pace, and being squeezed into a midfield role for which she is ill-suited significantly erodes her prospects here.|

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly is the sole confirmed pace-setter and won at this course and distance on her most recent start — Gavin Ryan can slot her straight to the front rail and control tempo, though her OR of 108 means rivals will be watching her closely and a style-fit flag reminds that sustaining her effort over the full six furlongs will be the key test.|

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has an excellent 6f record on Good ground and has won twice this season, making her one of the most proven horses in the field at this trip and surface; Pierre-Louis Jamin should be able to slot her into a prominent tracking position second or third, which is precisely where this race shape rewards.|

races.paceDynamic: Havana Anna is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other natural leader to challenge her for the rail, she can dictate terms at a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground over six furlongs at Naas. Dancing Saxon and Soul Love are the truest prominent types capable of tracking her through the race, with Dancing Saxon in particular likely to press from a handy position off the bend. The field is unusually front-heavy — Chantez, Treasure Rose, and Focaccia are all genuine prominent racers by nature but are mapped to midfield because there is simply not enough room for all of them to secure their preferred berth, meaning at least two will be shuffled wider or back than ideal. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting an honest but not suicidal pace — strongly favours horses who can race prominently in tracking positions and produce a sustained finish, rather than true hold-up types who need a stronger gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Havana Anna Controls, Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Anna dictates an unchallenged rhythm and kicks turning for home, her rivals are playing catch-up on a sound surface.
scenarios.body: Havana Anna's recent Naas win over this course and distance gives her a clear blueprint, and with no rival likely to press hard early she can conserve enough energy to repel challengers in the closing stages. Soul Love and Dancing Saxon, the two most natural trackers, are best placed to run her down if she ties up, but are unlikely to reel her in if she travels smoothly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Anna sets an honest enough gallop that the closest trackers can produce a sustained late surge to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Dancing Saxon's strong recent form — three wins from last five including successive six-furlong victories — puts him ideally placed just off the pace, and Soul Love's excellent 6f record on Good ground means both could pounce if the leader has emptied slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than anticipated and the race develops into a test that rewards genuine hold-up horses closing late.
scenarios.body: First Instinct is the only truly authentic hold-up type in the race with legitimate Group-level form, and a sound Good surface at Naas over six furlongs gives her a realistic closing window if the front-runners burn themselves off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the crowded prominent contingent manages to secure an unexpectedly handy position early and benefits from the pace dynamics ahead.
scenarios.body: Treasure Rose's two recent wins suggest she is in form and would thrive if she finds a clearer path than the race shape implies, while Chantez remains capable on Good ground though both are compromised by the congested prominent tier.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Chantez, Treasure Rose, or Focaccia clash for position in the early stages — if all three attempt to push forward simultaneously the pace could spike sharply in the opening two furlongs, transforming this from a controlled leader's race into a truly contested gallop that fundamentally alters the finish.|

Havana Anna is uncontested on paper but carries a STYLE_FIT flag — if Gavin Ryan cannot find a comfortable rhythm through the first two furlongs and she over-races on this Good surface, the energy cost could see her vulnerable inside the final furlong rather than kicking clear.|

First Instinct is 44 days between runs and has limited 6f form (her win came over 5f on Soft); if the pace is steady rather than strong, Cieren Fallon may find her closing run arrives too late to matter, making her reliance on a specific pace scenario a real concern.|

Dancing Saxon is the only three-year-old in the field with a realistic chance from a prominent role and is arriving at the weight allowance — monitor his early positioning, as if McDonogh can lock onto Havana Anna's quarters through the turn he is best positioned to deliver a winning challenge.|

Soul Love's trainer K.R. Burke has 7 winners from 38 runners in the last 14 days, giving the yard strong in-form claims — note that her four 6f Good-ground runs have produced three wins and a third, making the combination of surface and trip a significant form asset in this field.|

races.name: Big Evs At Tally-Ho Handicap

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Andrew McNamara who brings solid 5f and 6f Good-ground form including a recent third, and Sam Coen's 5lb claim offers a weight relief; needs a gap to open inside the final furlong, which is harder than usual with the field compressed.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and clear pace-setter over a trip and going where she has won and placed repeatedly; the visor helps her concentrate and she has to be respected as the race's tempo controller even if her OR of 60 is near the ceiling — the question is whether sustainable fractions are enough.|

runners_data.name: Menwirr
runners_data.note: Young Denis Hogan three-year-old returning from 89 days off, and the booking of 7lb claimer Mel Sheridan does not shout confidence; limited Good-ground form on this distance and stepping back to 5f from 6f-7f suggest this is an exploratory run rather than a winning mission.|

runners_data.name: Nebrook Star
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer with a win on Good and placed form at the trip, returning quickly off 8 days; the blinkers are noted and the 7lb claim from Jamie Orr lightens the load, though stable's one-from-five recent form deserves scrutiny.|

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old who is utterly at home on 5f Good, with 13 of his last 15 runs on similar going including a recent second; Chris Hayes is a high-quality booking and his course-specific record makes him one of the most interesting hold-up contenders in the field.|

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Drawn from a yard with no wins in the past six entries, and his form over 6f and 7f on Good and Soft raises questions about whether this 5f trip plays to his strengths; Ben Coen is a capable handler but the evidence for this horse winning here is thin.|

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's five-year-old brings a win over 6f Good and is being asked to go a furlong shorter; a genuine prominent type who should find the 5f trip suiting his quick early pace, though he has been racing at 6f recently and the style adjustment is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Pansy Poe
runners_data.note: A long 331-day absence is the dominant concern here regardless of style or going; ran respectably on 5f Good in previous seasons but ring rust after nearly a year off makes any positive conclusion premature — a hold-up horse who needs the fitness to last.|

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Holds a second on 5f Good in recent form but is a genuine hold-up type who fades in finishes — mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is overcrowded; the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.90) means his best-placed form is hard to reproduce from further forward than he would naturally choose.|

runners_data.name: Smart Sioux
runners_data.note: Also fades in finishes and is a true hold-up runner by nature, crowded out of his natural position at the back; the STYLE_FIT warning (0.91) is significant in a 5f sprint where he rarely settles at the rear and has no wins on Good ground at this trip — the profile does not fit the likely race shape.|

runners_data.name: Hasiyna
runners_data.note: Returning from 156 days off for John McConnell, whose yard has been busy (4 from 27 in 14 days); a genuine back-of-field runner whose best form came on Soft/Standard rather than Good, and being pushed forward out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.92) further dilutes her already thin credentials here.|

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Batt Burke with four places from 15 runs on Good, and the 7lb claimer Adam Browne-Souza takes the saddle; consistent at this level without ever winning but should travel comfortably in the first three or four — a solid shape fit for this scenario without necessarily being the winner.|

runners_data.name: Prada's World
runners_data.note: 484-day absence is an enormous flag and the horse's form prior to that showed no wins; returns on Good ground over a trip shorter than he has raced — a true rear-of-field type pushed forward by field compression (STYLE_FIT 0.92), making this look like a fitness-finding exercise.|

runners_data.name: Amanirenas
runners_data.note: Has a win on 6f Soft but that came almost a year ago and the 331-day absence matches Pansy Poe's concern; a natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.91), and while trainer Grassick has one recent winner, nothing in the profile suggests a winning return.|

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Two course wins on Good ground over 5f is the headline statistic — Rory Cleary takes the ride and the trainer has recent placed form; a genuine prominent type who should find his natural position just off the leader and represents one of the most credible pace-suit matches in the field.|

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Willie McCreery's four-year-old has five consecutive top-4 finishes over 5f including two on Soft and four on Good; W J Lee is a high-quality pilot, the visor remains in place, and this horse's profile of travelling close to the pace and sustaining the effort fits the anticipated race shape almost perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Little Roy
runners_data.note: A 70-day absence and only three career runs is the primary concern for Gillian Scott's three-year-old; Leigh Roche takes the ride but the horse has finished sixth or worse in all three starts, all on 5f-6f Good, and is mapped out of his natural hold-up position (STYLE_FIT 0.90) — the shape is not kind to him.|

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: Has finished 12th or worse in all four starts and wears a tongue-tie that has not unlocked improvement; the 7lb apprentice Robyn Donaghue-Leahy takes the ride but this is a horse with no form over any trip on Good ground and a true hold-up style that cannot be accommodated at the rear (STYLE_FIT 0.90) — the race shape offers no relief.|

runners_data.name: Lismacbryan
runners_data.note: Zoe McMullan's 10lb claim is a weight bonus for a horse returning from 87 days off; best form came on Soft/Standard and the hood goes on, but as a genuine rear-of-field type displaced by field congestion (STYLE_FIT 0.92), the combination of going, absence, and positional compromise leaves this runner with a lot to overcome.|

races.paceDynamic: Dandy Land is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 5f at Naas on Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into excessive fractions. I'm Spartacus, Whatswrongnow, Step Back In Time, and Steel Magnolia will press forward into prominent positions behind her, creating a compact early order rather than a true pace collapse. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent types than can occupy natural positions — Smart Sioux, Simmering Seas, Hasiyna, Lismacbryan, Amanirenas, Prada's World, Little Roy, and Niobite are all genuine rear-of-field horses who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, compressing the field and reducing the room for a late finishing burst. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured gallop with a wall of promoted hold-up horses crammed into midfield — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in the first three or four positions and sustain their effort through the final furlong, making the early-to-prominent racing profile the decisive tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandy Land Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land is allowed to control the pace entirely without being chased down, setting a rhythm that sees her through to the line.
scenarios.body: Dandy Land, already proven over course-and-distance, exploits a light weight and a clean passage to lead from flag to finish at a sustainable Good-ground gallop; her recent form string of 1-2-3 on 5f Good backs up her credentials to front-run and hold on here. Prominent types who can settle just off her shoulder — Steel Magnolia and Step Back In Time — are the primary threats, having shown repeatedly on 5f Good ground that they can sustain efforts launched from a forward position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land's unchallenged lead causes her to slow the early pace fractionally, allowing the horses positioned just behind to overhaul her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Steel Magnolia, with five consecutive top-4 finishes on 5f, and Step Back In Time, who owns two wins in similar 5f Good conditions, are ideally placed to cruise into contention and cut Dandy Land down without needing to produce a searching late burst. I'm Spartacus and Whatswrongnow, both genuine prominent types who know their way around competitive handicaps from this sort of position, add depth to the second scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield creates a gap in the final 100 yards and a horse travelling strongly from just off the pace manages to pick through.
scenarios.body: Tawaazon carries strong course-and-distance credentials, racing regularly over 5f Good at Naas with a recent second included, and represents the most credible genuine hold-up type who could find a seam if the prominent horses tie up. Aurora Nova has sound form at 5f on Good ground and, ridden by an in-form claimer, could also pick up pieces if the front rank fades, though the compressed field limits the available runway for a late charge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected challenger pushes Dandy Land into a hot early gallop that burns off the field and leaves the race wide open for a fresh-legged finisher.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because there is no confirmed second front-runner to force the pace, making a true collapse unlikely on Good ground over 5f with a lone pace-setter; however, should I'm Spartacus or Whatswrongnow push forward aggressively from the off and test Dandy Land, the early fractions could unravel and expose tired horses in the final strides. In this unlikely scenario, any horse that settled further back than mapped — including Tawaazon or a revived Simmering Seas — could pick up a race run in chaos.

watchPoints.text: Dandy Land breaks cleanly and builds her lead — watch whether any of I'm Spartacus, Whatswrongnow or Step Back In Time push forward to test her in the first furlong, because if none do, she could steal an unassailable advantage.|

Steel Magnolia is the horse to watch for position in the first two furlongs — if W J Lee can tuck her in second or third on the rail behind Dandy Land, her five-race recent form record of consecutive top-4 finishes over 5f on similar going becomes very relevant.|

The compressed midfield of genuine hold-up horses — Smart Sioux, Simmering Seas, Hasiyna, Lismacbryan — will be jostling for position from the off; watch for interference and knocked-about passages in the first furlong as they are forced to race out of their natural roles.|

Tawaazon is returning quickly and races off the pace — watch whether Chris Hayes can find a clear passage through a bunched midfield in the final 100 yards, because his 5f Good record is strong but gaps may not materialise

races.name: Hartes Group Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose one win came on soft-ish ground at the Curragh over a shorter trip; similar-going record of just one place from six runs is thin, and from 31 days off Ross O'Sullivan's yard will need to produce a career-best in a packed rear group to land this.

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: D.K. Weld's charge is the lone confirmed pace-setter and gets an uncontested lead, which is the key tactical asset here; OR=70 and a return trip within 8 days is a potential concern for stamina over 1m3f, but the race is hers to lose if she can see it out.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a genuine good-ground win in her recent form string and veteran headgear (visor) suggesting a specific trigger; trainer Gerard O'Leary sends her out 24 days fresh and she has placed four times on this going, making her one of the more dependable closers if traffic clears.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed in good-ground conditions before but whose last five runs include a cluster of mid-field finishes over slightly shorter; Seamus Fahey has had no runners in the 14-day window, so this comes cold, and the 1m3f stretch is worth watching.

runners_data.name: Derry Lad
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old wearing a tongue-strap who has finished fifth five times on the bounce over distances from 10f to 15f on good ground — a model of consistency without a win since likely long ago; from 17 days off, he plugs on but rarely threatens.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Maurice Ahern's six-year-old wears a tongue-strap and is a genuine hold-up horse whose best efforts have come at 10-12f on good ground, but the congested field means he is unlikely to find his natural deep position useful here; OR=63 and two place-finishes in six good-ground starts cap the ceiling.

runners_data.name: Maralinga
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes, which is a critical weakness in a compressed hold-up pack; the eight-year-old's last five runs are all over 16-17f, making this 1m3f trip a significant drop in distance that could theoretically suit — but the fade flag and 44 days off (Timothy Doyle, quiet yard) make this speculative.

runners_data.name: Parish Team
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's three-year-old has three runs in, all resulting in eighth or worse on good ground, and carries the fade flag; still, as a horse whose natural position appears slightly forward of the pack, a clean prominent run is the only scenario where the unexplored upside matters.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: P. Sweeney-trained seven-year-old who is a natural hold-up horse across a career at 7-10f — significantly shorter than today's 1m3f; the step up in trip is a major question, and a 38-day break with a yard that has had no recent runners adds cold-stable risk.

runners_data.name: Signor Ferrari
runners_data.note: P.J.F. Murphy's five-year-old has prominent-style form and the best-fitting profile for tracking Glittering Gem; one win from nine on similar going and a 34-day freshener from a yard that has placed one from nine recently suggests the talent is there if the trip (career-best territory) holds up.

runners_data.name: Tero d'Rosa
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse with a win and a place on good-to-firm/good, and his last good-ground runs show he handles conditions; mapped forward of his ideal position due to the redistribution, but from 42 days off the talent to run a big race is present if he slots in without interference.

runners_data.name: Amavasya
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground last time out at 79 days ago for M.C. Grassick, wearing a hood — the freshness and headgear combination is worth noting; a true closer who is pushed forward by the congested field, but a horse arriving off a win and with proven good-ground form is one of the stronger underlying profiles here.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's seven-year-old has form in extreme-distance races (16-18f), so dropping back to 1m3f is a sharp contraction; wears a tongue-strap, and while he placed over 18f on good going, the style mismatch on this shorter trip alongside redistribution out of his deepest position limits the appeal.

runners_data.name: Wie Wunderbar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Mrs John Harrington with only three runs and a style classed as unknown — a genuine wildcard; 72 days off and no going data make meaningful assessment impossible, but a fresh, well-bred unknown from a powerful yard can never be dismissed in open handicaps.

runners_data.name: Walls Cross
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading and carries the lowest OR in the competitive part of the field at 53; four runs on good ground have produced finishes of 8th-11th, and from 11 days off Timothy Doyle's quiet yard, this is a horse that will need exceptional circumstances to threaten.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old has placed twice over 11-12f on good ground and wears a phood — a relevant headgear flag; flagged for fading but shows the form profile of a horse who stays and could be competitive if pace judgement clicks, making him one of the more interesting younger closers.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Arrived off a win and has a string of placed efforts on good ground over 9-12f for Richard Brabazon; ran just five days ago which is a quick turnaround and may indicate connections feel the horse is in a purple patch — the form profile is solid if the bounce factor doesn't bite.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a form string of consistent double-figure finishes across good and standard going, flagged for fading; no trainer 14-day runners and a career best of 8th makes this a very difficult profile to recommend under any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Glittering Gem is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, critically, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — she can dictate a measured, controlled gallop over this 1m3f trip on good ground at Naas, conserving enough energy to remain a factor late. Behind her, the race is saturated with hold-up types: Maralinga, Covert Legend, Tero d'Rosa, God Of Thunder, Amavasya, God Knows and others are all natural closers, meaning the midfield and rear will be extremely congested and many will fail to secure their preferred position. Signor Ferrari and Parish Team offer the most plausible secondary cover just off the pace, while the redistributed hold-up horses are forced to race closer than their style dictates, which systematically undermines their finishing effectiveness. With a sustainable, uncontested pace set by one horse and the closers' pack too large and too compressed to generate a clean sweeping finish, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just behind the leader — those who can track a steady tempo, avoid traffic, and produce their effort early in the straight rather than weaving through a wall of horses in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gem Dictates, Prompt Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Glittering Gem sets an uncontested moderate gallop and horses tracking prominently produce their effort earliest in the straight.
scenarios.body: Glittering Gem controls fractions entirely unchallenged, and the runner or runners just behind her — Signor Ferrari, Parish Team — inherit the clearest ground turning for home; the hold-up pack is too far back and too numerous to reel in a horse that has saved petrol throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Split Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough to compress the field and a single hold-up runner finds a clear run to pounce in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: One of the better-credentialed closers — Tero d'Rosa or Amavasya — manages to avoid the congested rear pack and produces a sustained late run on a track where good ground favours horses travelling through the race; the key is whether a gap materialises late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Gem Weakens, Midfield Surges
scenarios.trigger: If Glittering Gem's solo lead catches up with her inside the final 2f and a horse tracking just off the pace inherits the race.
scenarios.body: Showyoutheropes or Sinbad My Dad, both hold-up types forced slightly closer than ideal given the redistribution, find themselves in range as the front-runner stops, and good-ground form here gives them a credible vehicle; the scenario still depends on these horses getting cleaner positioning than the rest of the compressed pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield creates significant trouble in running and a lightly-weighted or unexposed runner sneaks through on the rail.
scenarios.body: Wie Wunderbar, lightly raced and unknown in style, or Yquem — who has been running into form on this going — could benefit if chaos behind the pace creates an opening that a fresh pair of legs can exploit; this is a low-probability shape precisely because it requires both pace breakdown and a fortuitous path through traffic.

watchPoints.text: Glittering Gem sets the sole pace unchallenged — if she gets a soft opening 4f and conserves energy, horses committed to tracking her (Signor Ferrari, Parish Team) are best placed and the field's closers may simply have too much ground to make up.

The rear of the field is dangerously overcrowded with redistributed hold-up horses — Maralinga, Covert Legend, Tero d'Rosa, Amavasya, God Of Thunder, God Knows — and significant traffic trouble or interference is likely in the straight; watch for horses getting hampered between the 3f and 1f poles.

Amavasya is the only redistributed closer arriving off a recent win with headgear (hood) and a powerful trainer — if she slots in with cleaner running room than her stable-companions, she represents the biggest threat from the back group.

Yquem's five-day turnaround flags a yard that believes the horse is in form right now; the good-ground record over this trip range is solid, but a quick bounce is a real risk in a race this competitive.

Wie Wunderbar's unknown running style from Mrs Harrington's yard makes this horse a genuine variable — in a race where every other prominent slot is accounted for, an unexposed three-year-old with no public style profile could land anywhere in the first half of the field.

races.name: TRM BIOACTIVE Energy Boost Handicap

runners_data.name: Alice Monet
runners_data.note: D K Weld's filly is in excellent form — a winner at nine furlongs on good ground 18 days ago — and holds solid course-and-distance form; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is an asset, and she stays this trip well, though the moderate expected gallop may blunt the impact of her hold-up finish.|

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's three-year-old carries a 7-race losing run in this form but showed promise in a Group context earlier in the campaign; headgear (p) is fitted, she has good-ground credentials, and Jack Cleary's claim helps, but the hold-up style and 23-day break make her reliant on a stronger pace than Guardian Of Realm is likely to set.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's four-year-old is a winner over this exact trip and going combination, races prominently and will be positioned to strike turning for home; the trainer's low T14 strike rate (1/29) is a mild flag, but Shane Foley gives her a professional pilot and her form figures of 3-1-8-7-5-1 confirm she's in a productive vein.|

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on this JP Murtagh-trained five-year-old who was placed over today's trip on good ground last time; she races from hold-up, the 38-day break is notable, and the modest pace expectation means she needs things to open up neatly in the straight, which is not guaranteed.|

runners_data.name: Akecheta
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman's six-year-old has been running consistently in mid-division without threatening; the tongue-tie and headgear (tp) are familiar accessories, W J Lee takes the ride, and while he has good-ground form, his overall record (0W1P in similar conditions) suggests he is most likely to fill a minor place role at best.|

runners_data.name: Guardian Of Realm
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter and recorded his most recent win over today's trip on good ground; the 87-day absence is the single biggest risk factor, and though his STYLE_FIT score flags he is racing somewhat out of natural profile, he is likely to dictate terms and could prove hard to pass if fit.|

runners_data.name: Mocking
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the depth of the field means he cannot get to his preferred position at the rear; the 62-day absence and a form string that reads 4-6-6 since his last win make him tough to support, and Rory Mulligan's inexperience in big-field handicaps adds further caution.|

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: John Nallen's three-year-old is a dual winner — at eight furlongs and sixteen furlongs on good ground — who races prominently and appears well-placed in this field; Reese Holohan's 7lb claim reduces the weight, and the step back from extreme distances to one mile two and a half furlongs looks a sensible move.|

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Richard O'Brien's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up runner who will be unable to get to his natural position at the rear given the number of similar profiles in this field; an eight-day turnaround is a quick return, his good-ground form record (0W0P on similar) is uninspiring, and Andrew Slattery inherits a difficult tactical hand.|

runners_data.name: Speckled Meadow
runners_data.note: Don Browne's nine-year-old is a veteran hold-up type who arrives here 24 days after his last start, but age, an OR of 67, and a tendency to be out the back combine poorly with today's expected moderate pace; Julian Pietropaolo's 7lb claim helps the weights, though this runner faces the steepest task of any in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Guardian Of Realm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will settle into an uncontested, sustainable gallop over this mile and two and a half furlongs on good ground at Naas. Diamond Exchange and Akecheta will push forward to track closely in second and third, giving the race a calm, measured early tempo that is unlikely to truly test the pace-setter. The bulk of the field — Alice Monet, Port Of Spain, Ob La Di — will be held up in rear, needing the gallop to quicken sufficiently in the straight to deliver their finish. Three runners tagged as redistributed — Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow — are genuine hold-up types who cannot all get to the rear in this compact field and will be forced to travel in midfield against their natural instincts. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those just off the pace who can track the uncontested leader and pick him up efficiently, rather than deep closers who need a fast, searching gallop to produce their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Guardian Of Realm dictates a moderate, uncontested pace and the race is won by a horse tracking closely from the outset.
scenarios.body: Guardian Of Realm sets a comfortable fractions under Chris Hayes, with Diamond Exchange or Minella Rockett ideally placed to pounce entering the straight without needing a searching gallop to be delivered. This shape rewards horses racing within their natural style in the first three, as the race never truly tests hold-up types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses find enough daylight in the straight and the pace proves sufficient to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: Alice Monet is the most likely beneficiary, having won on good ground over this trip and possessing a powerful finishing effort when produced late by Sam Coen. Port Of Spain's Group experience gives her a class edge if she can be produced efficiently, though the moderate tempo makes this harder to execute.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Guardian Of Realm burns his rivals off too aggressively and ties up in the closing stages, opening the race wide.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the leader's stamina over the final two furlongs would see the midfield and rear horses swarm late, with Alice Monet and Port Of Spain the main threats if they can find clear runs. This remains a lower-probability shape given the steady, uncontested tempo that Guardian Of Realm is expected to control.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Muddle, Redistributed Runners Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield causes traffic and interference, shuffling the finish order unpredictably.
scenarios.body: Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow are all forced out of their natural positions and racing against type, increasing the risk of scrimmaging through the first half-mile and creating gaps that compromise true hold-up runners at the back. In this chaotic shape, Diamond Exchange's prominent position and experience at the trip could prove the decisive advantage.

watchPoints.text: Guardian Of Realm returns from an 87-day absence as the sole pace-setter — monitor his paddock condition and early market moves, as his fitness level is the single biggest swing factor in how this race is run and who benefits.|

Mocking, Quatre Bras, and Speckled Meadow are all true hold-up horses forced into midfield by the race shape — watch for scrimmaging and checking in the first half-mile that could compromise the runs of Alice Monet and Port Of Spain from the rear.|

Diamond Exchange races prominently and has a strong record at this trip on good ground, but her trainer's 14-day strike rate (1/29) is low — watch for any market drift that might signal the stable is not at its peak.|

The pace is expected to be modest and uncontested, which compresses finishing times — horses drawn or positioned to make smooth, unimpeded moves rounding the final bend will have a clear edge over those needing gaps to open late.|

Minella Rockett's jockey Reese Holohan claims 7lb, reducing what would otherwise be a competitive weight; watch whether that claim has been specifically engineered to get this horse competitive at the top of its handicap mark on a flat, sound surface.|
